pairs.old: - So "is of the Holy Ghost" says where the child is from. It does not say whose child he is; it is not "the Holy Ghost's child".
pairs.new:
- So "is of the Holy Ghost" says where the child is from. It does not say whose child he is; it is not "the Holy Ghost's child".
- Read it with the rows that use the same words, precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10). Matthew 1:20's "conceived ... of the Holy Ghost" is gennao (G1080) + ek (G1537) + pneuma (G4151) (kjv_word_map). John 3:5 and 3:6 use the same three words of the new birth:
  - John 3:5: "Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and [of] the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God."
  - John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
  So what is "of the Spirit" is spirit, not flesh; flesh is born of flesh.
- Matthew 1:18 has the same ek with the Holy Ghost (G1537 + G40 + G4151): "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- The lexicon's "by (the means of)" and "cause" senses of ek say from whom, or by whom, the child comes. Read with John 3:6, neither makes the Holy Ghost the begetter of flesh.
- John 1:13 gives ek four times: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- The word match supports reading these rows together. The rows decide, not the lexicon.

pairs.old: SUPPORT ONLY: John 3:5, 3:6, 3:8 and John 1:13 give gennao + ek with the Spirit, or with God, for the new birth. They are not womb rows.
pairs.new: SUPPORT ONLY: John 3:5, 3:6, 3:8 and John 1:13 give gennao + ek with the Spirit, or with God, for the new birth. They are not womb rows. Item (4) of the IN DEBATE head reads them beside Matthew 1:18 and 1:20, as support for reading those rows together.
